Hi Alex / Samantha —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and next steps from our side, plus a few procurement/billing questions so we can get a clean commercial path in place: 

Recap (short):
- Goal: Evaluate Redwood for inference serving (initial pilot: 2 dedicated nodes for search ranking)
- Timeline: pilot kick-off target: early August, production Q4 if pilot successful
- Success criteria: latency < 50ms p95, cost target <$0.05/token for bulk rerank workload

Procurement / billing questions (so we can produce the correct paperwork/invoice):
1) Payment method: do you prefer Purchase Order (PO) or corporate card for the initial pilot? If PO, is there an approval threshold (e.g., $10k+ requires PO)?
2) Net terms: do you require net-30 / net-45 / immediate? Any vendor credit setup required?
3) Invoice format: do you need line-item SKUs, tax/VAT ID on the invoice, or a specific PO number format?
4) Billing remit info: billing name, billing address, tax ID / VAT ID to appear on invoice
5) Marketplace: are you interested in procuring via Azure/AWS marketplace or do you prefer a direct vendor invoice?

Attached is a sample invoice and our W-9 to speed the procurement review (Redwood-Invoice-Sample.pdf, Redwood-W9.pdf).

Proposed next steps:
- Can you confirm procurement contact and preferred payment method?
- If PO is preferred, can procurement confirm the PO cadence and the email to receive invoices?
- If helpful, we can schedule a 20-min procurement call this week to walk through the sample invoice and required fields — is Thursday or Friday better?

Looping in Nikhil (finance lead) to help with any vendor setup questions.

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Short answers below and a couple of items for procurement: 

1) Payment method: For anything over ~$10k we go via Purchase Order. Small pilots under $10k can be paid by corporate card.
2) Net terms: Our standard is net-30 after invoice receipt; procurement can approve net-30 for pilots with approved PO.
3) Invoice format: We need a PO number on the invoice (we'll provide when we issue the PO). Invoices should include line items with unit price and quantity. No VAT for our US entity; we do need the vendor Tax ID on the invoice.
4) Billing remit: Our billing address is: Acme Corp, Attn: Accounts Payable, 123 Market St, Suite 400, San Francisco, CA 94103. Invoices should be emailed to invoices@acmecorp.com (please cc procurement@acmecorp.com).
5) Marketplace: We're generally open to Azure Marketplace, but procurement wants to lock POs for the pilot. Marketplace onboarding can be a follow-up once pilot is approved.

Procurement contact: Samantha Lee (samantha.lee@acmecorp.com) — she manages vendor setup and PO issuance. I'll loop her in.

Happy to join a brief procurement call if helpful; Thursday afternoon works for me.

Best,
Alex
Head of Product, Acme Corp

Hi Marissa / Alex / Nikhil —

Thanks — procurement here. Quick answers and what we need to issue a PO: 

What we need from Redwood to generate a PO:
- Vendor legal name exactly as it should appear on the PO/invoice
- Remit/billing address for Redwood
- Redwood Tax ID / EIN (we require a completed W-9 for US vendors)
- Typical invoice line itemization (SKU, description, unit price, quantity) — the sample invoice you sent looks good, please ensure line items are present
- Preferred invoice email (we will send the PO to that address)

Our preferences:
- PO number will be provided once we issue; please ensure your invoices reference the PO number
- Net-30 is fine
- Invoices should be sent to invoices@acmecorp.com and procurement@acmecorp.com cc'd
- For pilot amounts under $15k we can expedite; above that it goes through standard legal review which adds ~7-10 business days

We do not need VAT for the US entity. If you have marketplace listing details, please send them but we will proceed with direct PO for the pilot.

Once you confirm vendor name and remit address we will generate the PO and share the number. Happy to do a quick 20-min sync Thursday 3:00pm PT if that works for everyone.
